newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says bulk of unemployment fall genuine.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says bulk of unemployment fall genuine.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday the bulk of November's huge 95,800 fall in unemployment was due to economic growth.
But he told Reuters Financial Television that sweeping change to the benefits system including the new jobseekers allowance accounted for some of the drop.
"It's certainly had some effect, no-one knows exactly," Clarke said. "But it's so large this fall...that surely the bulk of it, 40-50,000 must have been a result of growth in the economy."
November's jobless fall was the largest on record and took the total number of unemployed below two million for the first time since early 1991.

Clarke said some people would have left the unemployment benefit claimant count, either because they shouldn't have been claiming benefit or because they didn't want to take advantage of what was offered to them under the JSA.
"We are seeing increased consumer confidence, more money being spent and falling unemployment," he said.
But he said there was little prospect of a boom. "Today's fall in unemployment...was combined with steady earnings figures."
Annualised underlying average earnings growth held steady at 4.0 percent in October.
"But I stand ready to act as I did two months ago, to do whatever is necessary to achieve the inflation target," he said.
Clarke raised base rates by a quarter-point to six percent on October 30.
